solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Beat victim, a sucker

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or beat
a prey is a victim of a hunter

explanation.surface: Someone who gets beaten up is a gullible mark, a sucker.
explanation.definitionFit: The lamprey is an eel-like fish that clamps onto prey with a round sucking mouth, so it is literally a sucker.

clue.text: Rely on eating British far from home here

indicators.note: eating means the reliance phrase takes in the letter for British

parts.note: to lean on is to rely on

explanation.surface: A Briton abroad depends on eating British food.
explanation.definitionFit: Lebanon is a Middle Eastern country, so a British visitor there is a long way from home.

clue.text: Truth, for Blair, was one error I'm about to test

indicators.note: about means the error and I'm pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a sin is a moral error
taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
to try is to test

explanation.surface: Tony Blair's version of truth was a mistake about to be put to the test.
explanation.walkthrough: Blair here is Eric Blair, George Orwell, whose Nineteen Eighty-Four has a Ministry of Truth, not Tony Blair. 'about' reverses SIN + IM to MINIS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orwell's novel the propaganda department is called the Ministry of Truth, so Truth was one government department.

clue.text: Come back to put penny in bank

indicators.note: in means the penny goes inside the bank word

parts.note: to bank on is to rely

explanation.surface: Someone comes back to deposit a coin in the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: To reply is to answer or retort, which is what come back means.

clue.text: Anything or nothing may unite, alternatively

indicators.note: alternatively means arranged another way, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: O, the zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: Anything or nothing could bring people together, as another option.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said after a list to mean whatever you like, every possible thing.

clue.text: Bird initially makes a sound like a crow

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word makes

parts.note: a caw is the harsh call of a crow

explanation.surface: A bird starts off by imitating a crow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: The macaw is a large brightly coloured parrot, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Unpretentious metre: poem is on the way

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A simple metre for a poem that is in progress.
explanation.definitionFit: A modest person or thing is humble and not showy, much like unpretentious.

clue.text: Double bend suggests trickery, with line removed

indicators.note: removed means the line letters are taken away

parts.note: chicanery is trickery
RY, railway, is a line

explanation.surface: A double bend in the road hints at deception once a line is taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: A chicane is a tight S-shaped pair of turns on a motor-racing circuit or road.

clue.text: Secure ends of cable and start back

parts.note: to win something is to secure it

indicators.note: ends of picks the first and last letters of cable

explanation.surface: Fasten both ends of a cable and then begin again.
explanation.definitionFit: To wince is to flinch, recoiling suddenly in pain or embarrassment.

clue.text: Way melon can make one sick

parts.note: a path is a way
an ogen is a variety of melon

explanation.surface: A dodgy melon you buy along the way could make you ill.
explanation.walkthrough: OGEN is a small sweet melon first bred in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: A pathogen is a germ such as a virus or bacterium, an organism that causes disease.

clue.text: Martyr's vestment some snipped

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is just the martyr

parts.note: an alb is a long white priest's vestment

indicators.note: snipped means the word for some loses its tail end

parts.note: some, as in 'have you any?', means any

explanation.surface: A martyr's robe has been partly cut away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snipped' trims ANY (some) to AN. Read 'Martyr's' as 'Martyr is'.
explanation.definitionFit: St Alban is honoured as the first recorded Christian martyr in Britain.

clue.text: Barred character quietly sounding off

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

indicators.note: off means going wrong, so the letters of sounding get mixed up

explanation.surface: A character with bars on is quietly making a noise somewhere off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' (the anagram signal) gives OUNDSIGN. 'Barred' suggests prison, but it is the stroke drawn across the £ symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The £ symbol has a horizontal stroke through it, so it is a typographic character with a bar.

clue.text: Truly, not large plant

indicators.note: not says the letter for large is left out

parts.note: honestly is a synonym of truly
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone insists, truly, that a plant isn't large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes the L out of HONESTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Honesty is a garden flower (Lunaria) grown for its silvery, coin-like seed pods.

clue.text: Some witches' death here in question

definitions.meaning: witches were often burned tied to a post, so this names where their death came
something in question is on the line, at risk

explanation.surface: Whether some witches died here is still a matter of doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something being decided or risked is said to be on the line, the phrase used for an issue under debate.

clue.text: I get friend to move to such an improved area?

definitions.note: the adjective describes the area rather than naming it

indicators.note: to move means the letters of the phrase are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone persuades a friend to relocate to an upmarket neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move' rearranges I GET FRIEND. The definition describes an area that has been upgraded.
explanation.definitionFit: A district that has been renovated and taken over by wealthier residents is described as having gone upmarket in this way.

clue.text: Blooming stumping we got for a duck

indicators.note: we got for a duck means the word we replaces the zero

parts.note: flooring someone, like stumping them, baffles them
a duck is a zero score in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a terrific stumping, and we got out for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got for' swaps one O of FLOORING for WE. In cricket a duck is a score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering plant is one in bloom, so the participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Water that's French, European — and English

parts.note: the French word for that, the water just named, is mer, the sea

explanation.surface: A lake described as being at once French, European and English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's French' refers back to 'Water': in French it is MER. Add E for European, and 'and English' notes the result is the English word for water.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a lake or pond, an old English word still used in place names.

clue.text: Put notice up about parts of film that are regularly over our heads

definitions.text: that are regularly over our heads

indicators.note: about means the reversed notice word goes around the film parts
in a down clue, up means the word for notice is written bottom to top

parts.note: to see is to notice
clips are short extracts of film

explanation.surface: Someone puts up a notice about film extracts that keep going over people's heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives EES and 'about' is the container signal. 'over our heads' sounds like something too hard to grasp; it means literally in the sky above.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclipses of sun and moon recur at intervals in the sky above us.

clue.text: A bet makes one nervous

parts.note: a flutter is a small bet, informal British

explanation.surface: Placing a bet makes a person jittery.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a flutter means being excited and anxious, so this is a synonym of nervous.

clue.text: Deeply involved, up to this kiss

definitions.meaning: someone deeply involved is said to be in it up to here, a phrase completed by a body part
to kiss and cuddle amorously, in informal speech

explanation.surface: Someone thoroughly caught up in an affair, up to the point of a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Being 'up to your neck' is an idiom for being deeply involved; to neck is slang for snogging.

clue.text: EU subsidy applied to Asian crop? Fancy!

parts.note: CAP is the EU's Common Agricultural Policy, its farm subsidy scheme
rice is a staple crop of Asia

explanation.surface: European farm subsidies paid for growing rice in Asia? Imagine that!
explanation.definitionFit: A caprice is a whim or sudden notion, and a fancy is a passing liking.

clue.text: Sort of mass fiction troubled friend consumes

indicators.note: consumes means the friend word swallows the other letters

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: troubled means stirred up, so the letters of fiction are mixed

explanation.surface: A friend is bothered by a lot of made-up writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' gives ONTIFIC, and 'consumes' is the container signal. 'mass' looks like a quantity but is the church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A pontifical mass is a High Mass celebrated by a bishop, so it names one type of this service.

clue.text: An appendix to one's Old Testament?

definitions.text: An appendix to one's Old Testament?

parts.words: An appendix to one's Old Testament?
parts.note: a testament is also a will, and a will written long ago may have an addition attached

explanation.surface: Is there an appendix to the Old Testament of the Bible?
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible is a decoy: one's old testament is a will made earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: A codicil is a supplement amending a will, which is a person's last testament.

clue.text: Realise murderer is keeping quiet

indicators.note: keeping means the murderer word holds the quiet letters

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone recognises that the killer is staying silent.
explanation.walkthrough: Cain, the first murderer in Genesis, is a standard crossword killer; 'keeping' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise an asset is to convert it into money, the financial sense of this phrase.

clue.text: Cause of trouble, a single place to enter craft

indicators.note: to enter means these pieces go inside the word for cause of trouble

parts.note: a bane is a source of trouble
I, the Roman numeral one, is a single

explanation.surface: A troublemaker gets into a craft by finding a single spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A biplane is an aircraft with two pairs of wings, and aircraft are craft.

clue.text: Plain is one, in degrees Celsius

indicators.note: in means the one letter goes inside the degree letters

parts.note: BAs, Bachelors of Arts, are university degrees
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Is the plain one measured in degrees Celsius?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I between BAS and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means simple and unadorned, without frills, so it matches plain.

clue.text: Teased with more intensity after injury

indicators.note: after places the intensity word behind the injury word

parts.note: a wound is an injury
up, as in turning the heat up, means with more intensity

explanation.surface: Someone was mocked even harder after getting hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind someone up is to tease or provoke them, so the past tense matches teased.

clue.text: Joker riding cart

parts.note: a wag is a joker
on, as in on horseback, means riding

explanation.surface: A comedian rides along in a cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a four-wheeled vehicle for carrying goods, a larger kind of cart.

clue.text: Fluorescent tubes trip out: insulting

indicators.note: out means the word trip is removed

parts.note: strip lighting is lighting by long fluorescent tubes

explanation.surface: The fluorescent lights trip out, and someone mutters rude remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes TRIP from STRIP LIGHTING. 'Fluorescent tubes' looks like the anagram fodder but is a phrase for STRIP LIGHTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Slighting remarks belittle someone, so the participle matches insulting.

clue.text: Some hair a persistent pain on end of foot

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word foot

parts.note: an ache is a dull persistent pain

explanation.surface: A nagging pain at the end of the foot, plus some hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tache is informal British for a moustache, a growth of facial hair.

clue.text: Cold meat free of fat, and sterile

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
lean meat has no fat

explanation.surface: Cold fat-free meat that is also germ-free.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean means free of germs or dirt, a near synonym of sterile.

clue.text: Cruel daughter died, one strangled with both hands

parts.note: gone is a euphemism for died

indicators.note: strangled with means the hand letters wrap around the one

parts.note: R and L are right and left, both hands
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A daughter died after being throttled by someone using both hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangled with' puts I between R and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Goneril is one of King Lear's two cruel elder daughters in Shakespeare's play.
